# lookout audit policy

Dump the effective posture rule table after merging detector defaults, --profile, --policy, and CLI overrides (--only, --skip, --min-severity, --set) so operators and agents can inspect what a scan will enforce before running it.

MCP tool: `k8s_audit_policy` (MCP profile: `audit`)

## Usage

    lookout audit policy [flags]

## Flags

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--policy` | — | path to a YAML posture policy file |
| `--profile` | — | built-in posture profile: default\|strict\|onboarding\|gke-autopilot |
| `--only` | — | comma-separated check kind or kind/reason globs to run exclusively |
| `--skip` | — | comma-separated check kind or kind/reason globs to skip |
| `--min-severity` | — | minimum finding severity to emit: info\|warning\|critical |
| `--set` | — | comma-separated check parameter overrides (<kind>.<param>=<val>) |

## Common flags (every lookout command)

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--namespace` | — | limit the scan to one namespace |
| `-A` | — | scan all namespaces |
| `--workload` | — | target one workload as <Kind>/<namespace>/<name>, e.g. Deployment/prod/api |
| `--since` | — | how far back to look (0 = command default) |
| `--format` | logfmt | output format: logfmt\|json (one record per line either way) |
| `--timeout` | 10s | abort the invocation after this long (exit 1) |
| `--kubeconfig` | — | path to a kubeconfig file, instead of $KUBECONFIG / ~/.kube/config |
| `--kubeconfig-dir` | — | directory of kubeconfig files to fan out across (mutually exclusive with --kubeconfig); each finding is stamped with cluster=<label> and the summary reports clusters=<n> |
| `--context` | — | kubeconfig context to read, instead of its current-context. Selects a cluster for THIS invocation only — nothing is written back — so concurrent invocations can target different clusters. Reported as context=<name> in the summary line |
| `--contexts` | — | comma-separated kubeconfig contexts to fan out across, or '*' for every context in the selected kubeconfig(s) (mutually exclusive with --context); each finding is stamped with cluster=<label> and the summary reports clusters=<n> |
| `--concurrency` | 4 | maximum concurrent cluster executions when fanning out with --contexts or --kubeconfig-dir |
| `--exemptions` | — | path to a git-reviewed exemption file (YAML); covered findings are ANNOTATED with their reason and expiry and counted as exempt=<n> in the summary, never dropped |

## Finding kinds

Every `kind=` this command can emit, and the severities it carries them at. Nothing else appears in its output; a kind absent from a run means the check looked and found nothing.

| Kind | Severity | Claim |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `audit.policy_rule` | info | the resolved enablement, effective severity, provenance layer, and threshold parameters for one posture check rule |

## Output fields

Beyond the shared envelope fields (`kind`, `severity`, `namespace`, `kind_of_object`, `name`, `reason`, `message`, `fingerprint`, `exempt_reason`, `exempt_expires`):

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `target_kind` | the posture check kind (`<kind>`) or reason (`<kind>/<reason>`) this rule governs |
| `enabled` | whether findings matching this rule will be emitted (`true` or `false`) |
| `effective_severity` | the severity findings matching this rule will carry after profile and policy overrides |
| `default_severity` | the detector's built-in severity before any profile or policy override |
| `source` | which precedence layer determined this rule (`default`, `profile`, `file`, or `flag`) |
| `params` | comma-separated `<key>=<val>` threshold parameters in effect for this check, when parameterized |

## Output contract

Output: one finding per line (logfmt; --format=json for one JSON object
per line), keys in fixed order; healthy resources emit nothing. The final
line is always the summary: scanned=<n> findings=<n> elapsed=<d> —
findings=0 with a summary present means "scanned and healthy"; a stream
without a summary line is void. Exit 0 data, 1 runtime error (diagnostics
on stderr only), 2 usage.

## Examples

```lookout
lookout audit policy
lookout audit policy --profile=strict
lookout audit policy --policy=policy.yaml --min-severity=warning
```
